Hi Karthik / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — ClearWave has a hard launch in Q3 and we want to be sure hosting costs don’t blow up as we scale. We ran some usage sims and we’re looking at ~1.2B tokens/month by month 6 if the pilot converts.

Can Redwood provide a committed tier or a per-token discount that sits below the published rate card for that volume? We’d prefer a usage-based commit rather than a heavy upfront reserved capacity commitment right now.

Key asks:
- A committed per-token price that applies up to 1.5B tokens/month (month-to-month billing)
- A capped overage rate if we spike above commitment
- Standard SOC2 + data residency confirmation (we’ll ask security separately)

Attached is our draft SOW and a simple volume model so you can see the math. We’re trying to get budgeting sign-off by 3/10.

Appreciate a quick read — happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Ava

Thanks for the context. Copying Sean for pricing / concession guardrails.

High-level guidance:
- We can consider a per-token concession for Volume >=1B tokens/month, but concessions at that scale need finance approval (tiered concession or timeboxed pilot concession).
- Prefer a 3-month ramp pilot with an evaluated true-up at the end of the pilot. That limits exposure.
- No below-baseline (floor) pricing — any concession must preserve minimum effective revenue (we’ll model against cost per token).

Please surface the following so finance can make a decision:
1) Expected month-by-month token ramp for 6 months (they included a model but ask them to confirm)
2) SLO / latency requirements and whether they’ll accept fallback to cheaper model variants on overload
3) Any committed duration (month-to-month vs 12m) they’re willing to consider

Karthik — please collect answers and loop in Legal if there are non-standard payment terms.

Looping in finance view after reviewing the model. Summary:
- ClearWave’s baseline model shows an effective unit cost (at published rates) that would exceed our target minimum margin at 1.2B tokens/month.
- We can approve a temporary concession for a 3-month pilot up to 1.2B tokens/month at a 15% discount off published per-token rate, provided the following conditions are met:
  * Pilot is timeboxed (90 days)
  * ClearWave pre-agrees to a one-time true-up if actual usage materially exceeds the model (>25% variance)
  * No minimum guaranteed revenue below $25k/month during pilot (to cover fixed infra/operational costs)
  * Any longer-term pricing requires a committed 12-month cadence or reserved capacity contract and new approval

Attachments: I added a simple break-even summary (pricing_model_breakdown.xlsx).

If Sales accepts, we can put these into a short amendment and route for Legal / Procurement. If Sales needs more concession, escalate to CFO (Marissa, please confirm escalation path).

Sean Gallagher
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference

Ava — thanks for sending the details and model. We discussed internally and can offer the following to move the pilot forward quickly: 

Offer summary (pilot):
- 90-day timeboxed pilot (starts on activation date)
- Up to 1.2B tokens/month covered at a 15% concession off published per-token rate
- Overage: standard published rate + 10% premium if monthly usage exceeds 1.2B tokens
- True-up clause: if usage >25% above the forecasted band during the pilot, ClearWave agrees to a one-time reconciliation payment
- Minimum revenue floor: $25k/month for the pilot period

Next steps:
1) If that works, Karthik will prepare a short amendment and SOW update — I’ve attached the SOW back with a cover note.
2) We’ll ask Legal to prep a short pilot addendum and route for signature (DocuSign link once ready).
3) Sean will review the true-up and finalize the break-even math — we’ve attached his spreadsheet.

If you’d like a quick call to agree on the pilot start date and activation criteria, Karthik and I are available tomorrow.

Regards,
